title: Junta Warships and Jets Hit Seven Villages Across Ponnagyun, Sittwe and Rathedaung Townships, Rakhine State
detail: Junta warships shelled coastal areas around Kyeintali and Ngapali in Thandwe District around 11:02 a.m. on September 3, 2026, before four jet fighters carried out roughly 30 minutes of continuous bombing runs beginning around 1:35 p.m. over villages at the border junction of Ponnagyun, Sittwe and Rathedaung townships in Arakan (Rakhine) State — including Kwun Taung, Kon Tan Kyein Chaung, Makka La, Nyo Yaung, Min Hla, Moe Se Kyein, Kyet Yoe Seik and Nyaung Pin Gyi. The wave broke a roughly month-long lull in bombardment around the state capital. The United League of Arakan (ULA) urged residents across Arakan State to maintain heightened vigilance for further air raids and naval artillery, warning attacks "could occur at any time."

media.caption: The United League of Arakan warned civilians of ongoing airstrikes and artillery attacks across Arakan State after the September 3 bombing wave.

title: Seven Surviving Junta Vessels Reach Bhamo With Fuel and Reinforcements After Losing Eight Vessels
detail: Two combat ships and five cargo vessels of the junta's battered Ayeyarwady River flotilla docked in Bhamo, Kachin State on September 3, 2026, after breaking through the KIA-PDF ambush along the Zinbon-Sinkhan stretch — completing a resupply run that began August 21 from Mandalay's Gaw Wein jetty with 15 vessels. Eight vessels were lost, sunk, damaged, or surrendered to resistance forces along the way. "If this flotilla hadn't made it, the junta troops here would have been in serious trouble," a Bhamo-based resistance fighter told BNI.

media.caption: Surviving junta vessels dock in Bhamo, Kachin State, after running the KIA-PDF gauntlet along the Ayeyarwady River.
